name: manual_5b857b
claim: RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme / JCS) defines canonicalization by sorting object keys by UTF-16 code units and formatting numbers per ECMAScript, whereas Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) operates over Unicode code points. While byte-identical over a restricted domain of ASCII alphanumeric keys and safe integers, specifications must state the exact deterministic rule rather than claiming general RFC 8785 conformance, avoiding divergences on non-ASCII keys or negative zero.

decisions.notes: 2026-10-20: Testing vectors in docs/vectors/dispatch-permit-v1.json confirmed byte-identity with rfc8785 package over our ASCII/integer domain, but key sorting diverges outside ASCII (UTF-16 code units vs code points) and on negative zero. Precise spec language avoids false conformance claims.
